info.name: Bratra Inbound (Service Bus)
info.description:
Send messages to the Bratra Integration Platform's inbound Service Bus queue (`bratra-inbound`).

Every request:
- Auto-generates a fresh SAS token via the pre-request script (HMAC-SHA256 in CryptoJS). Token TTL is 10 minutes — no need to refresh manually.
- Auto-generates a fresh `meta.messageId` (UUIDv4) and `meta.correlationId` (timestamped) so each send is idempotent and traceable.
- Sets the right Service Bus broker properties (MessageId, CorrelationId, Label) on the message envelope.

See `README.md` for setup + auth steps.

exec: // Generate a fresh SAS token (10-min TTL) + new messageId/correlationId for every send.
throw new Error('Missing variables. Set sb_namespace, sb_queue, sb_key_name, sb_key_value in your environment.');
const newMid = (typeof crypto !== 'undefined' && crypto.randomUUID) ? crypto.randomUUID() : pm.variables.replaceIn('{{$guid}}');

item.name: 1. Send valid Action order envelope (happy path)

request.description: Sends a valid `ActionOrderBatchV1` envelope. Expected: HTTP 201 from Service Bus, then within seconds a row appears in BC `bratraSalesOrderBuffers` (status `Pending`).
Same wire as request #1, with a stripped-down body for you to fill in. Useful for testing your own scenarios. Don't change `meta.name` unless you know which orchestrator you're targeting.

Sends an envelope with an unknown `meta.name`. Expected: Service Bus accepts (201) but the consumer dead-letters with reason `UnknownMessageName`. Use this to confirm DLQ behaviour without polluting the BC sandbox.

item.name: 4. Send multi-order batch (3 orders, fan-out test)

request.description: Sends one envelope with three orders (POs 4002845710, 4002845711, 4002845712). Expected: HTTP 201 from Service Bus; the Function fans out to three independent Durable orchestrations (instance IDs share the correlationId prefix and differ by poNumber); three distinct rows appear in BC's `bratraSalesOrderBuffers` with externalIds `BRA-AC-{messageId}-4002845710/4002845711/4002845712`. Each row processes through the Job Queue independently — one failing does not affect the others. The 3 rows also have visible differences in `Contract Number`, `Unloading Location`, and `Quantity` so they're easy to tell apart on the buffer list page.
